summary: End-to-end backend + frontend regression for SAMAJ CONNECT Phase-2 (Firebase). Ran 13 pytest cases against live Firestore-backed API (auth token exchange via Firebase, samaj isolation, visibility authorization, conv membership, live cross-samaj, public-feed toggle, live-start validation) — all pass. Ran Playwright flows on preview URL for login (admin + member), Social (post/like/comment/save/share/menu/tabs/search/stories bar), Live (create/start with YouTube URL, iframe embed, react, chat, end), Admin dashboard (4 tabs, toggle-public-access, toggle-approval-default per samaj), Messages (new-chat search + direct convo create + navigate to /messages/{cid} + chat-input), Samaj switcher, Language toggle (gu<->en), member visibility select restricted to samaj/private (2 options as expected). No blocking bugs found.

issues: Console spam: '@firebase/firestore Could not reach Cloud Firestore backend. Connection failed 1 times.' The listener auto-reconnects and features still work, but the noise obscures real errors. Consider suppressing benign transient warnings or ensuring the preview environment can maintain a stable Firestore websocket.

action_items: No blocking action items. Optional: mute or downgrade the transient Firestore 'unavailable' console warning to reduce noise in DevTools.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_live.create_live allows creating a live session with empty streamUrl for 'created' status (no scheduledAt). Consider validating streamUrl at create-time as well, not only at /start, to match the UI contract 'no fake live'. Currently /start correctly rejects when streamUrl is empty (tested).
LiveRoom Player initial state shows an empty <div className='skeleton h-64'/> until GET /live/{lid} resolves; on slow networks this looks like a hang. Consider a labeled loading state.

Firestore listeners (listenMessages/listenLive/etc.) run directly from browser using client SDK; if Firestore rules deny or the browser is offline, users silently lose realtime updates while REST reads still succeed. Consider surfacing a small 'reconnecting…' indicator.
server.py dev_login always creates a Firebase user if not found — good, but there is no rate-limiting; keep DEV_AUTH_ENABLED=false in production.
